title: LightKG: Efficient Knowledge-Aware Recommendations with Simplified GNN Architecture

problem.claim: Knowledge Graph-aware Recommender Systems face sparsity issues, and incorporating self-supervised learning can lead to longer training time.

gap.claim: Existing GNN-based KGRSs fail to maintain superior performance under sparse interactions even with self-supervised learning, while greater model complexity and attention mechanisms can worsen sparse-scenario performance or increase learning difficulty.

contributions.claim: LightKG is a GNN-based KGRS designed to address sparsity issues.
LightKG uses a simplified GNN layer that represents directed relations as scalar pairs and applies linear aggregation to reduce GNN complexity.
LightKG uses an efficient contrastive layer for self-supervised learning that directly minimizes node similarity in the original graph without subgraph generation and comparison.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets reportedly show that LightKG outperforms 12 competitive KGRSs in sparse and dense scenarios while reducing training time.
LightKG reportedly exceeds the best baselines by an average of 5.8% in recommendation accuracy.
LightKG reportedly saves 84.3% of training time compared with KGRSs using self-supervised learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are described as the dominant approach for knowledge graph-aware recommender systems.
Self-supervised learning is used to address sparsity but leads to longer training time.
The authors report that existing GNN-based systems lose their advantage under sparse interactions and that added complexity can be detrimental.
LightKG combines simplified relation encoding and linear aggregation with an efficient contrastive layer for self-supervised learning.
The authors report improved accuracy and reduced training time across four benchmark datasets and 12 competing systems.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that more complex models and attention mechanisms can perform worse or increase learning difficulty in sparse interaction scenarios.

interpretation.claim: Under sparse data conditions, reducing model complexity may improve robustness and optimization behavior.

application.claim: When designing recommender systems for sparse interactions, evaluate simplified architectures alongside more complex mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that simplification is preferable for all datasets, tasks, or interaction densities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not describe the evaluation protocol, baseline configurations, or statistical variability.
The abstract does not provide detailed architectural equations or implementation settings.
